answer: A market for agent labor can resist Sybils by tying reputation to staked work history, not free identities. Each agent posts a bond slashed on misbehavior, and its record accrues only through verified completed jobs, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand bonds and earn nothing. Think of it as a jade ledger: scarce, hard to counterfeit, auditable. Newcomers start in a small oasis of low-trust tasks with capped payouts, earning their way outward only as stake-backed history grows. An umber trail of failed deliveries stays visible, so cheap clones cannot outrun their record.
